title: Nilo-Saharan languages - Wikipedia
text: The Nilo-Saharan languages are a proposed linguistic family consisting of around 210 Native African languages spoken by somewhere around 70 million speakers, mainly in the upper parts of the Chari and Nile rivers, including historic Nubia, north of where the two tributaries of the Nile meet.

title: Bagirmi | Traditional Culture, Ethnic Groups & Music | Britannica
text: Bagirmi, people living on the southern fringe of the Sahara, close to the region of Bornu in Chad and Nigeria. They numbered about 70,000 at the turn of the 21st century. Most speak Bagirmi, a Central Sudanic language of the Nilo-Saharan language family.

title: Bagirmi language
text: Bagirmi, also known as Baguirmi or Ɓarma (autonym: tàrà ɓármà; ISO 639-3: bmi), is a tonal Central Sudanic language of the Nilo-Saharan family, spoken by approximately 44,800 people (1993) primarily in the Chari-Baguirmi Prefecture of southern Chad.
